title: Beautiful, and Not
label: ch:ml-beauty
canDo: I can say that something is beautiful, name beauty itself, and deny it.

payoff.summary: From cold: both ends of one quality, and which letter arrives when aaNu follows a word.
payoff.note: Three atoms. THE FIRST DRAFT UNIFIED TWO DIFFERENT PROCESSES -- 'a letter arrives' is false for the anusvara, which already IS the m and only changes how it is written, and true only for bhangi/kutti where a ya is genuinely added between two vowels. It also taught that alla does not weld, read out of ML-C77's single chillu-final example, the one host that cannot show the rule; alla welds exactly as aaNu does and the headword is now ithu sundaramalla. The recall's 'nothing else' was falsified by its own title romanization sundaravum. ithu bhangiyaaNu means THIS IS BEAUTIFUL, not 'this is beauty'. The romanization is bhamgi, since the track reserves the nga letter for nga and writes a medial anusvara with the dotted m, as in kumbham. ROUND TWO OF REVIEW CAUGHT A FALSEHOOD IN THE FIX ITSELF: the correction explained that chapter 77's njaan adhyaapakan alla looks separate BECAUSE the host ends in a chillu, 'a consonant with no vowel to pass on'. That is false and two lessons the learner has already seen refute it -- ML-C36-makan has ithu ente makanaaNu and ML-C87 teaches adhyaapakane, the same word with the chillu going back to na. The chillu goes back to its full letter when a VOWEL follows, so the true version reinforces two earlier chapters instead of contradicting them. Also reverted an over-correction: the headword gloss was changed to 'beautiful' when bhangi is a noun, 'beauty' -- only the SENTENCE means 'this is beautiful'. And the glide is now credited to ML-C70-um, which already taught it at ariyum, rather than presented as new. ROUND THREE CAUGHT THE REPLACEMENT OVERSTATING. Calling the chillu 'the same trick as the anusvara' and conditioning it on 'the moment a vowel arrives behind it' is FALSE OF THE ANUSVARA: -um is vowel-initial and veLLam + um gives veLLavum, not *veLLamum -- and this chapter's own recall says eight lines away that what attaches matters. The two share exactly one join, before aaNu and alla, and the lesson now says so and warns against carrying it across. It also now cites ML-C87-accusative, which TEACHES the chillu rule on this same word, rather than only ML-C36-makan, which merely contains the form -- the same under-citation that was fixed for the ya glide and missed for the chillu. THIRD INSTANCE OF UNIFYING THINGS THAT LOOK ALIKE. ROUNDS FOUR AND FIVE. Round four found that 'once anything follows it' was itself false: a chillu reverts only before a VOWEL, because it cannot carry one, and ningngaLkku keeps its chillu before kku. The earlier text had the condition right and the unification wrong, and the fix had deleted the true half with the false one. Round five then found the chapter citing ML-C87-accusative by name while that lesson still taught the POSITION rule -- 'the shape a consonant takes at the end of a word' -- which predicts *ningngaLikku. ML-C87 was narrowed to the vowel condition using the corpus's own reason from the script lessons. Tracked in HL-C401; ML-C70-um-more still carries the same over-generalisation and is open.
